as_told.title: War of the Worlds broadcast panic

plain: This is an idea about why the US government kept UFOs secret after the Second World War. In 1938 the actor Orson Welles broadcast War of the Worlds, a radio drama about an invasion from space. Kirk McConnell, who worked as a staff member in the US Senate, says that in the late 1940s the country was barely ten years past that broadcast. John Harrington, speaking in an official role, puts it more bluntly: Welles broadcast War of the Worlds and the country went nuts. The point both make is that officials may have feared a similar panic if they admitted something real was in the skies, so they chose secrecy.
